delivery:
Reverse-engineered the Thomson-1-Large stack from the Thomson Reuters / Oxford team's own literature and landed it in FM-os as spec-as-data, runnable tooling and a scored forecast ledger.

KNOWLEDGE BASE (data, not prose)
- data/thomson_stack.yml — 18 pipeline stages, each with mechanism, owner, primary source and an evidence tier (published 14 / stated 4 / inferred 0).
- data/predictions.yml — 12 pre-registered claims with probabilities and resolution criteria, registered 2026-08-13 against the promised technical report.
- data/papers.yml +14 papers (ADMIRE-BayesOpt, SIMoE, CoLoR-Filter, CapTrack, Composable Interventions, Memory of Amortized Contexts, Knowledge Graphs for training data, Principal Hierarchies, Scales++, DeCE, Measuring What Matters, Every Eval Ever, PRISM, LingOly, GLEAN, HalluLens) under two new topics.
- data/people.yml +11 researchers under a new eval-science category, each mapped to the MECHANISM they own. Two names tagged in the post are deliberately absent (no public technical trace) under no-evidence-no-entry.

THE THREE FINDINGS
1. The org chart is the architecture. Bean is Evaluations Lead FOR LLM post-training — eval and post-training are one team. That is FM-os's own thesis ('eval gates are training-signal factories') as an external existence proof, now cited in RESEARCH-PROGRAM.md.
2. 'Minimal impact on other aspects' is a mechanism claim: SIMoE puts domain knowledge into separable sparse parameter subsets; CapTrack shows preference optimization is more conservative than instruction tuning and can partially recover. Schwarz's pre-Thomson career is continual learning — he was hired for exactly this.
3. The moat is the corpus and the editors, not the recipe. Every mechanism is published. Westlaw/Practical Law/Checkpoint/Reuters (<10% used) and 174 years of bar-admitted attorney editors are not. Reported scores confirm the shape: instruction following 0.914 and long context 0.753 best-in-class, LegalBench 0.823, Harvey Legal Agent 0.857 — but coding 0.399.

AGENTIC TOOLING
- skills/eval-subset (certified 98/100) — item-centric evaluation-subset selection, stage E1 made runnable. 2000-item benchmark, 100-item subset, 36 runs: item-centric mean MAE 0.0316 / p90 0.0363 at ZERO seed-model runs vs model-centric 0.0326 / 0.0356 at 40 runs vs random 0.0375 / 0.0452. Gates on p90 (tail risk), not the mean. Ships a falsifier that destroys the feature signal and asserts the edge vanishes. Two honest gate failures kept in the source.
- scripts/thomson.py + make thomson — validates both files and enforces the core rule: an 'inferred' stage must carry a registered bet. Brier scoring excludes unresolved predictions rather than crediting them.

COMMUNITY
Every Eval Ever (arXiv:2606.14516, Bean among 49 authors; 22,235 models, 2,273 benchmarks, 31 formats) named as the contribution target instead of founding a new forum. NOTHING SUBMITTED YET — recorded as open.

VERIFICATION
make validate + make thomson + 81 pytest passed + README/router drift clean + ainative 100%. One pre-existing failure (campaign checkpoint 'independent-5s-review', due 2026-08-11) fails on a clean tree and is untouched — Paul's gate to resolve.

HONEST LIMITS
Qwen 3.5 397B is single-sourced to the post (TR says only 'open source LLMs'); stage ORDERING is our reconstruction; no stage is confirmed to be in Thomson-1 — publishing a method is not shipping it, and that gap is exactly what the ledger measures. eval-subset numbers are synthetic-benchmark numbers, not a Scales++ reproduction.
